reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a perfectly flat, zero-valued signal across all scales, with no detectable periodicity, trend, amplitude modulation, peaks, troughs, or noise. All four reference candidates—spanning 1, 3, and 5 estimated periods (13, 39, and 65 points respectively)—exhibit identical morphology: a constant line at robust-standardized value 0.0, with zero median, zero MAD, zero roughness, zero curvature, and zero slope per point. This indicates an absence of any dynamic structure; the signal is static and deterministic within measurement precision. The stability is absolute: no drift, no jitter, no transient excursions. Given the robust standardization (median/MAD), this implies the underlying raw values in these intervals are constant (or nearly so) relative to the global median and MAD. Acceptable variation is effectively zero—any deviation from exact flatness at this scale would constitute an anomaly. The consensus across disjoint temporal segments (early, mid, late) confirms this is not a local artifact but a persistent channel behavior. While the dataset metadata suggests a weak cubic trend globally (R²=0.575), these reference excerpts show no trace of it, implying the trend is either negligible over short windows or has been fully removed by robust standardization. Thus, normality here is defined by perfect stationarity and constancy.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer the shortest reliable reference (index 0, 1P) for high-resolution query matching when only 1–2 cycles are visible; use index 1 or 2 (3P) for queries spanning ~30–40 points to assess multi-cycle consistency; use index 3 (5P) only when query length ≥60 points and long-range flatness must be verified. Since all candidates are identical, any may serve as proxy—but shorter windows reduce risk of incidental contamination in future unsupervised settings.
